text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 2.8% in two days (October 1–2), driven by a sharp rally in crude oil prices and refinery utilization hitting 92.5%—near full capacity. The stock has climbed $28.82 from its September 25 low, suggesting investor appetite for refiners when crude is strong and plants are running hot. Refiners profit from the spread between crude costs and finished fuel prices, so tighter refinery capacity and higher oil demand both favor their margins.

The broader backdrop remains volatile: geopolitical tension in the Middle East (tanker strikes near Iran, U.S. military posture) is keeping crude elevated, while the G7's announced 100 million barrel diesel reserve release could theoretically weigh on fuel prices. Today's modest gain reflects this tug-of-war—the refinery strength and tight capacity are winning out for now, but the risk of oversupply from strategic reserves hangs in the background.
